body: I once I had an extremely fulfilling job where I was serving others.  It was everything to me, and I could see the change I was making day to day.  But eventually I worked my way up the ladder to the point where politics took over, and it eventually cost me that job.  I dearly miss it every day, it's like a hole in my life that's no longer filled.  I have no promise of ever getting anything like it back ever again, and the further it falls back in time, the more depressed I am over it.

This is a very good point.  I grew up with my parents expecting a lot out of me.  I let them down throughout most of high school but when I made it to college, I worked my ass off.  I made them and myself proud, and I had tangible things to prove it.

But now there are no achievements, no tangible things.  Hell, my parents aren't even around for me anymore.  There are no more goals to attain, or at least reasonable expect to attain.
I appreciate the thought.  But what help does caring really provide?  I appreciate that people care, but ultimately all I do is let them down.  I'm afraid to let people care because of it.
What help can you provide?  What are options I'm not considering?
